Use the online retailer trick to get a free key.

1. Preorder a copy of the game for any platform you want (this does not force the beta code on the platform you chose, so you could preorder for one system and redeem the beta for another).

2. Check your email, you'll get your beta key there.

3. Redeem the beta key through the game's beta site.

4. Once redeemed and linked to your account, cancel the preorder with the online retailer.

So there you go. The retailer doesn't charge for preorders until the game releases, which is why this works.

There is also a massive enthusiasm for defending this game. As someone who tries to be as unbiased as possible, here's my perspective.

I was initially excited for this game. Played the early versions on a gaming console, and bought it on release day because I liked what I had already experienced. I went into it and completed the "story," and what a disappointment that was. The creators of a beloved franchise, known for its memorable narrative that I still appreciate today, produced that? The storyline was genuinely poor.

I found the gameplay itself excellent. Combat was enjoyable, and you didn't have to focus all your attention to perform well. It had a very casual, feel-good gameplay style that definitely worked in its favor.

But the thing I disliked most about this game: the lack of content. There was hardly anything. The environments offered no depth, just a fresh coat of paint with little to no areas to explore. Not to mention they were very underwhelming in size. The story was not only laughable but also brief.

The only highlight of the game? The cooperative challenge. And in my honest opinion, the game wasn't worth grinding through the same mediocre content repeatedly to experience that one highlight. One thing I've been told in response to this criticism was, "the expansions added a bunch more content!" Oh, give me a break. If I have to pay over a significant amount to get the content that should've been there at launch, there's a problem.

This is why people are skeptical about the sequel. Honestly, I want the second game to be good, and I want the developers to learn from their obvious mistakes. There's so much potential, but if it's anything like the first game, there will be a huge problem.
